discovery: Circuit quantum electrodynamics: strong coupling of superconducting artificial atoms to microwave photons
motivation: In 2004 Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf proposed coupling a superconducting qubit to a one-dimensional on-chip microwave resonator. The same year Schoelkopf's group demonstrated strong coupling, the vacuum Rabi splitting of a single artificial atom and a single photon. This 'circuit QED' brought the physics of cavity QED onto a chip, at coupling strengths that atomic systems cannot reach. Later experiments resolved photon-number states, made a quantum bus between qubits, and produced Schrödinger-cat states and bosonic error-correcting codes. Dispersive readout through the resonator, combined with quantum-limited Josephson amplifiers, gave high-fidelity, quantum non-demolition measurement of macroscopic circuits. That measurement architecture is now used in essentially every superconducting quantum processor. The work turned the demonstration that Josephson circuits are quantum into a precise laboratory for light-matter interaction and measurement theory. Theory and experiment advanced together in exemplary fashion.
